title: [M4][SM-405] Cross-browser WebGPU functional parity gate
body:
## Objective
Prove the feature-complete M0–M4 WebGPU renderer is functionally correct across the supported Windows browser targets before final performance/default-backend promotion.

## Scope
Chrome/Firefox WebGPU runs; API/resource validation; deterministic fixture captures; moving-light overlap review; device-loss/fallback; editor/room-transition tests; procedural parity; WebGL2 compatibility; browser-specific defects and evidence.

## Non-goals
- No final GTX 1650 Super performance/default-backend promotion; that is SM-505.
- No new rendering features or opportunistic visual tuning beyond parity/correctness defects.
- No release packaging decision beyond proving browser functional behaviour.

## Dependencies / concurrency
Depends on M0–M4 runtime correctness work: SM-100–104, SM-200–207, SM-300–307, and SM-400–404 as applicable. It may run before the final SM-501 performance gate. It blocks SM-505 final promotion.

## Canonical context
Read `docs/WEBGPU_VALIDATION_PLAN.md`, `docs/DEPENDENCY_AND_CONCURRENCY.md`, and `AGENTS.md`.

## Implementation prompt
Run the functional/visual validation matrix in Chrome and Firefox on supported Windows hardware. Prove boxes/control parity, corrected bin overlap behaviour, canonical procedural lighting, editor/runtime invalidation, device-loss/error handling, and WebGL2 fallback. Record unavailable tests honestly. Do not change `Auto` to WebGPU-first in this issue.

## Acceptance criteria
- Validation Gates A–E from `WEBGPU_VALIDATION_PLAN.md` pass or any remaining blocker is explicitly documented.
- Chrome and Firefox WebGPU functional runs complete on supported Windows hardware.
- Box/crate/barrel/cabinet/robot/pipes/water/foliage controls match or exceed WebGL2 parity.
- `binsright`, `binsleft`, `binsupleft`, and `binsup` meet the documented ownership/DSO/Dark-Bloom intent using authoritative references where available.
- Device-loss/initialization failure does not leave an unexplained black canvas and WebGL2 fallback remains playable/editor-capable.
- Editor and room-transition ghost-state regressions pass.

## Verification
Clean checkout/build/deploy; fresh browser profiles where practical; full deterministic fixture matrix; moving-light sweeps; inherited suite; WebGPU validation suite; Chrome/Firefox reports.

## Expected artifacts
`docs/WEBGPU_FUNCTIONAL_PARITY_VALIDATION.md`, browser/environment metadata, reference captures/debug dumps, defect fixes/tests discovered by validation.

## Blocking / stopping conditions
Any unresolved validation error, black-canvas/device-loss defect, visibility/ownership regression, procedural-light incoherence, editor ghost state, or browser-specific functional blocker keeps this gate open. Target-hardware timing alone is not a blocker for this functional gate; it is owned by SM-501/SM-505.
